question: When does a registered cancer-screening outcome support feasibility, assay performance, mortality benefit, or personalized cure—and when does it support none of them yet?

study.name: The Vanguard Study: Testing a New Way to Screen for Cancer

feasibility_primary: Proportion of participants who complete baseline and follow-up questionnaires within 60 days of receipt
Proportion of participants who provide the required blood sample for year 1 for Multi-Cancer Detection (MCD) testing within 90 days of recommended time point
Proportion of participants considered lost to follow-up within 2 years of randomization
pathway_and_harm_secondary: Timely return of MCD test result
Factors contributing to lack of diagnostic resolution of an abnormal MCD test
Diagnostic resolution following an abnormal MCD test result
Participation in standard of care screening
Complications related to diagnostic evaluation of an abnormal MCD test result
assay_performance_secondary: Accuracy of tissue of origin prediction
Sensitivity of clinical diagnostic performance of each MCD assay
long_term_other: Early and late stages cancer diagnosis
Targeted cancer-specific mortality of each MCD assay
Estimated costs associated with MCD testing minus estimated costs associated with standard of care screening
participant_burden_other: Proportion of participants who complete the Military Exposure Questionnaire

claim_ladder.name: operational_feasibility
claim_ladder.minimum_evidence: completed registered primary feasibility outcomes with prespecified denominators and numeric success thresholds

claim_ladder.name: diagnostic_pathway_and_harm
claim_ladder.minimum_evidence: resolved and unresolved abnormal-test pathways, time to resolution, procedures, complications, anxiety, contamination, and standard-screening participation

claim_ladder.name: assay_performance
claim_ladder.minimum_evidence: prospective sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, interval cancers, false positives, tissue-of-origin accuracy, and complete cancer ascertainment

claim_ladder.name: clinical_utility_and_mortality
claim_ladder.minimum_evidence: completed randomized arm-specific estimand with adequate follow-up, prespecified multiplicity and power, mortality ascertainment, and joint benefit-harm accounting

claim_ladder.name: personalized_treatment_or_cure
claim_ladder.minimum_evidence: treatment-specific randomization, molecular assignment rule frozen before outcomes, comparative treatment outcomes, toxicity, recurrence, and survival

go_no_go_threshold_rule.definition: A numeric go/no-go threshold must state an explicit cutoff or inequality for the endpoint measure itself. A measurement window, estimated enrollment, or reference to unspecified trial goals is not a success threshold.
go_no_go_threshold_rule.promotion_rule: Do not call the feasibility gate passed until denominators and numeric success thresholds are public and results are posted.

required_before_promotion: follow-up aligned to the registered time frame
false-positive, diagnostic-procedure, overdiagnosis, anxiety, and cost accounting

compare: passive follow-up duration in the detailed description
timeline_sentinel.rule: A long-term outcome cannot be promoted while the registered completion calendar does not span its stated follow-up horizon.

frozen_source_retention.compression: gzip with mtime=0 for deterministic bytes
frozen_source_retention.hash: SHA-256 over every retained source file

pilot_disclosure.boundary: Pilot inspection established the current outcome titles, study status, arm structure, outcome categories, and timing fields. No participant data, assay result, diagnostic outcome, cancer stage, death, or treatment outcome was inspected.

controls.positive: Every registered outcome must map exactly once to one frozen evidence class.
controls.negative: A synthetic claim that enrollment feasibility proves mortality reduction or personalized cure must be rejected.

next_gate: Publish numeric primary feasibility success thresholds and a timeline-aligned analysis plan; keep assay performance, diagnostic burden, mortality, and treatment claims in separate estimands.
interpretation_boundaries: This packet audits public protocol semantics and endpoint-to-claim alignment only.
It does not recommend an MCD assay, screening decision, diagnostic procedure, treatment, or trial participation.
It does not analyze participant-level data or compare the two MCD assays.
It does not establish mortality benefit, personalized treatment, cure, regulatory authorization, or a solved frontier.
